tools.description:
Ask the experiment analyst; returns text, typed charts, tool steps and PNGs.

Wraps the v1 chat agent (a smolagents ToolCallingAgent over the run's
posterior draws + mappings) which does segment filtering, WTP, clustering,
and posterior-plot interpretation, with up to 10 agent steps. Reports tool
progress during execution. Conversation history persists per user+run and
is shared with web chat; pass reset_memory=True to start fresh. PNGs are
presentation only; numeric tool outputs remain authoritative. May incur
model inference costs.

tools.description:
Compare 2–6 explicit conjoint scenarios against a named baseline.

Use the same 1–10 stable product IDs in every scenario, with every mapped
attribute specified. Product order may differ. Discover exact labels with
get_analytics_metadata first. opt_out is reserved for the model's opt-out.
Returns conditional preference probabilities and deltas, exact input/artifact
digests, counts and limitations. No LLM, vision, launch or paid experiment call.
Neither demand nor revenue/profit nor confidence in a commercial winner is
inferred. Concept studies and unavailable respondent artifacts are refused.

null_levels.description: When true, every attribute gains an injected `Not available` level, which raises the largest level count and changes the design. Send false explicitly when the design must contain only the submitted levels or when `not offered` is not a real option.

tools.description:
Find your owned studies in bounded, eventually consistent cache pages.

Query matches a literal title substring, ignoring case. Date bounds are
inclusive; dates without a timezone use UTC. Results sort by creation date,
type and ID descending. Reuse the same filters and limit with next_cursor;
restart if the cache changes. Missing caches mean incomplete coverage.
Artifact availability is unverified; status may be stale. No live provider
scan or experiment launch occurs. Concept studies need concept-specific reads.

returned only; no durable artifact is stored and no paid experiment is launched.

selection_extraction_model.description: Legacy field retained for saved-request compatibility; unused. Fast normalizes explicit choices deterministically without an extraction model.

experiment_type.description: Experiment methodology to run. Conjoint is the default first-release MCP path.

is_private.description: Whether the resulting W&B run should be hidden from other users.

anyOf.description:
Canonical market-ontology ids behind a draft's design labels.

Rehoboam never mints these: the host reads them from an accepted causl-kb
MarketSnapshot and records which one. A draft without a binding is still
valid; its results then carry no canonical reference. The canonical
example and its validators live in market-ontology
(`docs/examples/rehoboam-mcp-market-binding.json`, market-ontology#361).

items.description:
One design attribute (or respondent trait) bound to a canonical record.

The label is what the design says; the id is what the market says. A
label never implies a type: `Price` may be a manipulated Attribute in one
binding and a respondent Trait in another, and the two are different
records with different roles in the estimate.
One design level bound to a canonical AttributeLevel or TraitLevel.

population.description: Required explicit audience selection. Empty populations are rejected.

external_personas.description: External persona identifiers or URLs. Mutually exclusive with population_group.

anyOf.description: Exact non-US filters accepted by the population count validator.

non_us_target_population.description: Typed non-US demographic filters used for validation and execution.

population_group.description: Named population group to use. Mutually exclusive with external_personas.

anyOf.description:
Named US populations a caller can select instead of spelling out
demographic constraints. Each resolves to a TargetPopulation with at least
one real constraint, so the run takes the bounded marginals-then-sample
path every constrained run takes (see Prepare_Population's guard on an
all-empty target, which exists because an unconstrained run fans out over
the whole frame until the worker is killed).

population_preset.description: Name a stored US population instead of writing target_population. us_general_adults resolves to adults aged 18 to 99 across the twelve representative states the worker uses when no state is given. Counts as the demographic mode, so it can carry population_traits but cannot be combined with target_population, non_us_target_population, population_group or external_personas.

population_traits.description: Modeled traits keyed by trait name, for example {'Travel frequency': ['Weekly']}. Traits enrich selected respondents and do not select a population: pair them with target_population or non_us_target_population, or name a population_preset, or start_experiment returns 422.

anyOf.description: Exact US filters accepted by both draft validation and execution.

age.description: Inclusive [low, high] age range in years, for example [18, 65].

education_level.description: Allowed education levels; a respondent matching any listed value is eligible.

gender.description: Allowed genders; a respondent matching any listed value is eligible.

household_income.description: Inclusive [low, high] annual household income range in USD.

number_of_children.description: Allowed number-of-children buckets; a respondent matching any listed value is eligible.

racial_group.description: Allowed racial groups; a respondent matching any listed value is eligible.

state.description: Single US state to draw from. Omitted: twelve representative states.

target_population.description: Typed US demographic filters used for validation and execution.

priority.description: Which worker tier runs this study. `high` routes to the `high_priority` queue and `default` to the `default` queue; each has its own dedicated worker, so `high` never queues behind `default` and `default` is never starved. Omit for `high`.

why_prompt.description: Research question or decision the experiment should answer.
examples: What factors drive consumer choice of electric vehicles?

tools.description:
Confirm and start at most one paid run for the exact specification.

A trusted MCP elicitation shows the normalized specification and its
SHA-256 digest to the user. Acceptance is recorded in the durable approval
store before dispatch. Reusing the same idempotency key returns the same
reserved run and never submits a second paid experiment.

idempotency_key.description: Stable caller-generated key for this intended launch. Reuse the same key for retries; a different specification with the same key is rejected.

advanced.description: Reviewed experiment-design fields. Unknown internal controls are rejected.

add_neither_option.description: Adds an opt-out row to every task, so 2 alternatives become 3. Opt-out does not reduce the respondent draw. Keep true when uptake or demand is the question; set false for a forced choice.

alternatives_per_task.description: Profiles shown per choice task. None (default) lets the attribute-count heuristic choose; set 2..6 to show exactly that many, as a replicated study did. The opt-out row is added on top when add_neither_option is true. Fewer alternatives raise the respondent draw; 2 is the standard forced-choice format.

attribute_count.description: Number of attributes. 5-7 is the literature norm; above 9 the task exceeds what respondents can weigh.

confidence_level.description: Reported band derived from the fitted R-squared after the run. It does not set the sample size.

design_seed.description: Seed for the choice-task design. None (default) generates a fresh design every run; set it to repeat the design.

deterministic_stages.description: True runs the pre-survey LLM stages (latent variables, persona bios, mood statements, decision strategy) at llm_temperature instead of a fixed 0.7.

experiment_size.description: Population only: K=400/800/3200 in ceil(K * maximum levels / (tasks * actual alternatives)). Omitted keeps K=500. Does not change task design.

latent_variables_from_run.description: Name of a previous run whose latent-variable bundle (artifact experiment_latent_variables_<name>) this run reuses, so respondent prompts repeat. Requires the same population.

level_count.description: Levels per attribute. 3-4 recommended. The largest level count scales the respondent draw (ceil(K x levels / (tasks x actual alternatives)), with K set by experiment_size or 500 when omitted.

llm_temperature.description: Sampling temperature for the survey step. 0.0 is the default and the only comparable setting.

null_levels.description: When true, every attribute gains an injected `Not available` level, which raises the largest level count and changes the design. Send false explicitly when the design must contain only the submitted levels or when `not offered` is not a real option.

population_seed.description: Seed for drawing the synthetic population. The same request and seed draw the same respondents.

pre_cooked_attributes_and_levels_lookup.description: Closed-world design: `[[attribute, [level, ...]], ...]`. Submitted levels are used exactly as sent and are never reclassified as continuous; only `Not available` can be added, via `null_levels`. Each level names one exact value of one attribute, with units (`$14`, `14 days`, `12 oz`). Reject compound levels such as `$14 with Premium Blends` and ranges such as `$10-15`; they confound the part-worth of the attribute.

resample_population.description: True draws a fresh population on every run instead of honouring population_seed.

respondent_dependent_variable.description: Exact choice instruction shown to respondents. A nonempty supplied value is measured content and must not be rewritten.

response_contract.description: Survey answer contract. cot_json is today's chain-of-thought JSON; short is the trimmed template with one final JSON line of choices.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-provided key durably bound to this subject and specification.

wandb_run_name.description: Human-readable W&B run name generated by the backend.
